subject: ss-nephrology
title: Transplant immunology and histocompatibility: HLA, crossmatch and antibodies

steps.tx: The **human leukocyte antigen** system is the major histocompatibility complex in humans. Its genes lie on the short arm of chromosome 6. Class I molecules pair a polymorphic alpha heavy chain with **beta2-microglobulin**, which is encoded on chromosome 15 and is invariant. Class I molecules are expressed on nearly all nucleated somatic cells and present cytosolic peptides to CD8 T cells. Class II molecules are restricted mainly to antigen-presenting cells and present endocytosed peptides to CD4 T cells.
steps.say: The human leukocyte antigen system is the major histocompatibility complex in humans. Its genes lie on the short arm of chromosome six. Class one molecules pair a polymorphic alpha heavy chain with beta two microglobulin, which is encoded on chromosome fifteen and is invariant. Class one molecules are expressed on nearly all nucleated somatic cells and present cytosolic peptides to CD8 T cells. Class two molecules are restricted mainly to antigen-presenting cells such as dendritic cells and B cells, and present endocytosed peptides to CD4 T cells.

steps.tx: Peptide processing differs between the two classes. Class I peptides are generated by the **proteasome** and transported into the endoplasmic reticulum by TAP. **Calnexin** holds the new heavy chain in the rough endoplasmic reticulum until beta2-microglobulin binds. Class II peptides are handled in endosomes, where the **invariant chain** blocks the peptide groove until it is cleaved away.

steps.tx: Allorecognition has two routes. In **direct** recognition, recipient T cells see intact donor HLA on donor cells. In **indirect** recognition, recipient T cells see donor peptides presented on recipient HLA. A second signal is also needed: a **costimulatory** receptor on the T cell must engage its partner ligands on the presenting cell, otherwise the T cell becomes anergic. **Donor-specific antibodies** drive antibody-mediated rejection.

steps.tx: Pretransplant immunological risk is assessed with **panel reactive antibody** (PRA) and the **calculated PRA** (cPRA), which estimates the percentage of donors expected to be incompatible. The **single antigen bead** assay detects specific antibodies and gives quantitative values. A **complement-dependent cytotoxicity** crossmatch and a **flow cytometry crossmatch** test directly for donor-reactive antibodies against donor lymphocytes. A positive donor-specific antibody result usually leads to avoiding that donor.

steps.tx: **ABO-incompatible** transplants are possible when antibody titres are reduced before surgery, using plasma exchange, rituximab and IVIG. Graft outcomes depend on titre control and monitoring. Cold ischaemia time runs from perfusion stopping to reperfusion, and it should be kept short because prolonged storage raises the risk of delayed graft function. Ensure that donor-recipient crossmatch results are confirmed before any transplant decision.
